commonDocuments.title: Company Registration
commonDocuments.detail: Certificate of incorporation, GST registration, IEC (Importer-Exporter Code) and the legal address of the manufacturer and every production site.

commonDocuments.title: Product Datasheets
commonDocuments.detail: Current datasheets for every model and size in scope: nominal sizes (DN), pressure ratings (PN/MOP), temperature range, media and intended application.

commonDocuments.title: Technical Drawings
commonDocuments.detail: Dimensioned general-arrangement and sectional drawings with part lists, revision status and tolerances. All wetted parts must be identifiable.

commonDocuments.title: Material Specifications
commonDocuments.detail: Material designation (EN / ISO / ASTM) for every component, especially wetted metals, elastomers, plastics, coatings and lubricants, with supplier declarations.

commonDocuments.title: Quality Certificates
commonDocuments.detail: ISO 9001 certificate and scope, quality manual, and mill test certificates (EN 10204 3.1) for raw materials.

commonDocuments.title: Existing Test Reports
commonDocuments.detail: Previous type tests, hydrostatic and leak-tightness tests, endurance tests, and any approvals already held (e.g. WRAS, ACS, KIWA, NSF, BIS).

commonDocuments.title: Manufacturing Process Documentation
commonDocuments.detail: Process flow chart, control plan, work instructions, and a list of critical processes such as casting, machining, welding, moulding and assembly.

commonDocuments.title: Product Images
commonDocuments.detail: High-resolution photos of each product type, nameplate and marking, packaging, and cut-away or exploded views where available.

commonDocuments.title: Inspection Records
commonDocuments.detail: Incoming, in-process and final inspection records, calibration status of measuring equipment, and non-conformity handling records.

commonDocuments.title: Factory Information
commonDocuments.detail: Site address, layout, production capacity, key machinery, in-house test facilities, organisation chart and the contact person for audits.

categories.name: Valves
categories.summary: Gate, ball, butterfly, check and pressure-reducing valves for drinking water supply, and building installations.

standards.title: Valves for water supply – fitness-for-purpose requirements and verification tests
Manually operated copper-alloy and stainless-steel ball valves for potable water in buildings
Copper-alloy stop valves for potable water in buildings
Industrial valves – pressure tests, test procedures and acceptance criteria
German Environment Agency hygiene criteria for materials in contact with drinking water (organic materials and metals)

testFocus: Material hygiene of wetted parts (elastomers, coatings, lubricants)
preparation: Define the exact product range in scope: types, DN sizes and PN classes. Group them into product families for efficient type testing.
Compile a bill of materials for every wetted component and check each material against the UBA positive lists.
Freeze the design. Changes after test samples are sent usually trigger re-testing.
Run in-house pre-tests (shell, seat, torque) to the target EN standard before sending samples to an accredited laboratory.
Prepare product marking that meets the standard and leaves space for the certification mark.
mistakes: Using elastomers or lubricants without drinking-water hygiene evidence. This is the most common reason samples fail.
Submitting drawings without revision control, or drawings that do not match the samples.
Grouping too many variants together, so the laboratory requests additional samples.
Underestimating the cycle-endurance tests, which can take several weeks.

standards.title: Polyethylene (PE) piping systems for water supply – pipes
Plastic piping systems in water distribution – pipes made of PE 80 and PE 100
PVC-U piping systems for water supply – pipes
Ductile iron pipes, fittings and accessories for water pipelines
Stainless-steel pipes for drinking water installations
Composite pipes in drinking water installations

testFocus: Slow crack growth / resistance to point loads (PE)
Hygiene of pipe material and linings
extraDocuments: Compound / resin supplier approvals and data sheets
preparation: Confirm that your resin or compound already holds the required hygiene and material approvals. Certified compounds shorten the process considerably.
Define the dimension series (SDR / pressure classes) and select representative sizes for type testing.
Set up batch traceability from raw material to the pipe marking.
Validate in-house release tests such as melt flow rate, dimensions and hydrostatic tests, with calibrated equipment.
Prepare the factory production control documentation for the initial inspection.
mistakes: Switching resin suppliers during certification without notifying the certification body.
Marking that leaves out required information such as material, SDR, production date or batch.
Missing calibration records for the hydrostatic test rigs.
Underestimating long-term tests: some hydrostatic tests run for 1,000 hours or more.

categories.name: Fittings
categories.summary: Press, compression, threaded and electrofusion fittings, and pipe connectors for drinking water installations.

standards.title: Pipe connectors and pipe joints in drinking water installations
Copper and copper-alloy plumbing fittings
PE piping systems for water supply – fittings
Plastic piping systems in water distribution – fittings made of PE
Approved metallic materials (for example certain brass alloys) for contact with drinking water

testFocus: Joint tightness under pressure and vacuum
extraDocuments: System compatibility matrix (pipes, tools, press contours)
preparation: Specify the complete jointing system: fitting, pipe type and pressing tool or contour. Approvals are often granted per system.
Check every brass alloy against the UBA list of approved metallic materials. Lead content is critical.
Prepare samples across the full size range for pull-out and temperature-cycling tests.
Document the installation instructions in German or English as required.
Align the product marking and traceability with the certification requirements.
mistakes: Using brass alloys that are not on the UBA approved-materials list.
Testing fittings without defining the compatible pipe and tool system.
Missing dezincification test results for brass in water contact.
Incomplete installation instructions.

categories.name: Pumps
categories.summary: Centrifugal, submersible, booster and circulation pumps that come into contact with drinking water in supply systems and buildings.

standards.title: Hygiene requirements for all wetted materials: impellers, casings, seals, coatings
Pumps and pump units for liquids – common safety requirements
Rotodynamic pumps – hydraulic performance acceptance tests
Ecodesign requirements for water pumps (minimum efficiency index)
EU machinery safety and CE marking requirements, which apply in parallel

testFocus: Material hygiene of all wetted components
extraDocuments: CE declaration of conformity and technical file
preparation: List every wetted material, including small parts such as O-rings, wear rings and lubricants.
Confirm that coatings and elastomers come from suppliers with drinking-water approvals.
Align hydraulic test data with ISO 9906 acceptance grades.
Prepare the CE technical file in parallel. German customers expect both.
Identify a representative pump size for each hydraulic family.
mistakes: Overlooking minor wetted components such as gaskets and lubricants in the hygiene assessment.
Coatings applied by sub-contractors without documented process control.
Performance curves that are not backed by calibrated test-bench data.
Treating DVGW and CE as interchangeable. They cover different requirements.

categories.name: Water Meters
categories.summary: Mechanical and static (ultrasonic or electromagnetic) cold-water meters for utility billing and sub-metering.

standards.title: Measuring Instruments Directive – metrological conformity of water meters
Water meters for cold potable water and hot water
Volume and flow meters in water supply – selection, sizing and installation
Hygiene of wetted meter materials
German Measurement and Verification Act and Ordinance (national implementation)

testFocus: Metrological accuracy across the flow range (Q1–Q4)
extraDocuments: MID type-examination certificate (Module B) or plan for obtaining it
preparation: Clarify the regulatory route: MID conformity (through a notified body) is mandatory, while DVGW certification adds hygiene and suitability evidence that German utilities expect.
Prepare metrological test data across the full flow range.
Document the wetted materials, including the register, measuring chamber and seals.
For static meters, prepare software and EMC documentation early.
Plan the quality-system module (Module D or F) alongside product testing.
mistakes: Assuming DVGW certification replaces MID approval. It does not.
Insufficient durability test data.
Missing documentation of software versions for static meters.
Late involvement of the notified body.

standards.title: Mechanical filters for drinking water installations (80 µm to 150 µm)
Water softeners for drinking water installations
Test procedure for assessing the effectiveness of scale-prevention devices

testFocus: Performance and effectiveness (filtration, softening capacity, UV dose)
Hygiene of resins, membranes and housings
preparation: Define the claimed performance precisely. Testing verifies exactly what you claim.
Collect approvals for all treatment media, resins and membranes.
Document regeneration, disinfection and maintenance procedures.
Verify the backflow-protection concept against EN 1717.
Prepare German-language operating instructions for the end user.
mistakes: Making performance claims that are not supported by test data.
Using treatment media without drinking-water approvals.
Neglecting microbiological growth risks in stagnation zones.
Incomplete maintenance instructions.
